origins: The need for approval often begins with parents whose love seemed conditional, frequent criticism, or rejection by peers. A child who learns that keeping others happy keeps them safe may grow into an adult who can’t say no, avoids conflict, and feels crushed by any disapproval. Social media can intensify the hunger for likes and praise.
teaches: Paul asked whether he was seeking the approval of people or of God, and concluded that pleasing people could not be his goal. Proverbs warns that the fear of man is a snare, but trusting the Lord brings security. Scripture calls us to work wholeheartedly for the Lord rather than for people. God already approves of His children in Christ. That approval frees us to love and serve others without needing their applause, and to accept that not everyone will be pleased with us.
self_statements: If someone is upset with me, I’ve failed.
I need people to like me.
I worry constantly about what others think.
I’ll go along to keep the peace.
errors: Treating someone’s disapproval as a disaster.
Taking others’ moods as a judgment on me.
questions: Whose approval did I need most growing up?
Is it possible for anyone to please everyone?
What am I afraid will happen if someone disapproves?
Whose approval matters most, and do I already have it?
What have I given up to keep others happy?
Where could I be honest even if someone is not pleased?
truth: I care what people think, and that is human. But I cannot please everyone, and I don’t need to. God already accepts me in Christ. His approval frees me to be honest, say no when I need to, and love others without needing their applause.
hw_truths: I live for God’s approval, not man’s.
The fear of man is a snare.
God already accepts me in Christ.
I can say no and still be kind.
log: Each day, write one time you did something mainly for approval, and one time you acted on your own convictions.
actions: Decline one request this week that you would normally accept to avoid disapproval.
Express a different opinion respectfully in a safe setting.
Each time you change your behavior to win approval, ask, “Whose approval am I seeking?”
Read Galatians 1:10 each morning and remind yourself that God already accepts you in Christ.
tracker: A time I acted on my convictions
prayer: Lord, I have spent so much energy trying to please everyone. Thank You that I already have Your approval in Christ. Free me from the fear of man, and help me live honestly and lovingly for You. Amen.
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I must have everyone’s approval.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
